status: Native Python heap foundation verified locally and unreleased; public Python contexts and production delivery remain pending.

ownership.interpreter: RustPython owns the retained interpreter, scope, globals, closure cells, module cache, environment dictionary and output buffers. No guest globals are serialized to JSON and no source history is replayed.
ownership.checkpoint: PythonGuest park/resume stores and consumes one native handle in an isolated Wasm instance; the fixture uses the existing saveMemoryPages/restoreMemoryPages owner and native Alchemy R2. Metadata carries the exact metered runtime digest.
ownership.execution: begin rejects unfinished execution, validates the next program limits/environment, refreshes the owned environment and output buffers, and clears the prior terminal result. Fuel/page limits remain with the existing Wasm instrumentation owner.

checks: The first execution creates a genuine nonlocal Python closure and yields a host request; the fixture supplies response 2. begin is rejected while that coroutine is pending.
The second Worker restores the heap and retains the lexical cell and original /first.py code filename. A cached reference to os.environ sees MODE=second and removal of OLD.
A retained sys.stdout.write method writes only the second execution output. The third Worker evaluates the same closure to 43 with empty stdout/stderr.
Restored native handles can be consumed only once. All three snapshots use actual verified R2 pages and each original Worker is disposed before its replacement starts.

buildRecovery: The initial Wasm build found a cached Python bootstrap referencing a removed temporary checkout. Targeted cargo clean -p cirro-python --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release regenerated that package; the complete build and checks then passed. No dependency/vendor source was edited.
openGates: Public Python context selector, context-language contract and explicit migration.
Public ownership/authorization, deadlines, failure/reset/delete/collection and Queue/cron integration.
Dedicated negative proof of the reused-runtime freshness guard and broader module/coroutine checkpoint behavior.
Publication, deployment, actual Minutei Python consumption and production performance/cost evidence.
